- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-period, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment volatility is high (e.g., sentiment change >0.67) — increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% to account for momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment shows clear reversal signal.
- When news volume is constant (3.0) and sentiment is stable, model tends to drift toward historical mean — apply mean-reversion correction if forecast deviates >1.5% from 14-day moving average.
